description: Confirm-code pairing (ProjectInfo/04-PROTOCOL.md section 4.3, ADR-031). A = phone (initiator), B = PC (responder). Fixed keys are the RFC 7748 section 6.1 Alice/Bob pair, so pkA, pkB and the shared secret are published values.

algorithm.code: d = SHA-256("veyro-sas-v1" || pkA || pkB || nA || nB); code = BE32(d[0..3]) mod 1000000, zero-padded to 6 digits
algorithm.bootstrapKey: HKDF-SHA256(ikm = X25519(sk, peerPk), salt = nA || nB, info = "veyro-pair-confirm-v1" || idA || idB, L = 32); ids are the 26-character DeviceId strings, US-ASCII

verification: Generated by a standalone Python 3 reference (hashlib/hmac plus an RFC 7748 Montgomery ladder) written from the spec, independent of both clients. The generator first checked itself against RFC 7748 6.1 (public keys, shared secret), RFC 5869 test case 1 and both identity/device-id.json vectors.
notes: The code has a leading zero, so zero-padding is exercised.
Only pkA, pkB, nA, nB and the ids enter the derivations; device names and endpoints never do.
A commitment computed with any other nB, pkA or pkB must not verify; the phone aborts and stores nothing.
The code and nonces are never logged by either client.
